hypothesis: The parent caps *how high* the per-bin density weight can grow (4x median) but leaves the masked_scatter update free to push hot-bin weights *downward* to 1e-12 whenever `density_weight_new` is small, and — more importantly — the cap is applied to every bin uniformly, so bins that are already at the cap get no relief while the global weight keeps climbing. Instead, make the per-bin cap adaptive to the *spread* of the current per-bin weights (cap at median + k*IQR-like spread), so hot bins in a congested region are throttled relative to their peers rather than by an absolute multiple of the median, which should reduce regional detours that inflate TNS.
expected_effect: TNS improves on all three (regional congestion relief → fewer moderate violations); WNS roughly neutral to slightly better; overflow unchanged or slightly lower; runtime unchanged.
analysis: The hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with robust score +0.172 and no invalid runs. Largest gain on bp_fe-ng45 (score +0.275, dWNS +32.1%, dTNS +24.1%), consistent with adaptive spread-based capping throttling hot bins relative to congested peers, reducing regional detours and TNS inflation. Overflow rose modestly (~96–126), suggesting a mild density/legality tradeoff worth monitoring. Next step: sweep the spread multiplier k (e.g., 1.0–2.0×IQR) across seeds to confirm the TNS gain persists without overflow regressions, and check whether the 1e-12 downward floor is still needed under adaptive capping.
